advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Fix the 'two outcomes' wording at SKILL.md:160 to match the three status cases actually enumerated (or collapse to link-vs-resume framing consistently).
evidence: SKILL.md:160: `- \`Step 0(a): duplicates <id> (<alias>)\` — a match exists. Which of the two outcomes you take`
SKILL.md:162-167 lists three cases: '**Open or in progress**', '**Closed, and the behavior is back**', '**Closed, and it is the same still-live behavior that was never actually fixed**'
advisory.finding: The duplicate-handling prose says the choice is between 'the two outcomes' but then enumerates three distinct status-driven cases (Open/in-progress → resume; Closed & behavior back → regression/file+link; Closed & never fixed → reopen/resume). The '(one of) two outcomes' count contradicts the three bullets that follow.
advisory.suggested_fix: Change 'Which of the two outcomes you take' to 'Which outcome you take' (or 'Which of the three outcomes'), so the count matches the enumerated cases.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Either use `_heading_line` to enforce single-occurrence of the Step 0 / Phase 1 headings, or remove the unused helper.
evidence: No call site: the sole heading-locating tests (test_step_0_precedes_phase_1, test_step_0_applies_to_the_fast_path_too) use inline `next(...)` / `startswith` rather than `_heading_line`
advisory.finding: The test defines helper `_heading_line` (with its own assertion that a heading appears exactly once) but no test calls it; it is dead code.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Strengthen test_raw_nanosecond_before_form_is_absent so a raw 19-digit --before value in any spelling fails (e.g. regex for --before="?[^@] followed by a digit run, or a positive assertion that every --before= in the file is of the @$(( .../1000000000 )) form).
evidence: The docstring claims to guard: 'the raw form silently returned the tip of main instead of a floor' — but only two literal spellings are checked.

SKILL.md line 172: '**A rebar ticket carries **no version field**' and line 175 uses 'rebar --version' (space, not hyphen) — the checked hyphenated token appears nowhere, so the negative is trivially satisfied.
advisory.finding: test_raw_nanosecond_before_form_is_absent guards the reintroduced-bug case by enumerating only two exact string spellings (--before="<created_at>" and --before="$created_at"), so a raw-nanosecond form reintroduced in any other spelling (single quotes, a different placeholder, an inline value, or no quotes) passes the check vacuously. The absence oracle cannot distinguish 'the broken form is gone' from 'the broken form came back in a spelling I didn't list'.
merged_from: test_no_ticket_rebar_version_field_is_referenced asserts the literal 'rebar-version' is absent, but the skill never uses that hyphenated token in any form (it uses 'rebar --version' and 'no version field'), so the assertion is near-vacuous: it holds against essentially any plausible SKILL text and cannot catch an agent being told to read a nonexistent ticket version field spelled any of the natural ways (e.g. 'version field', 'ticket.version', 'rebar_version').
advisory.suggested_fix: Replace the two literal-negatives with a regex that asserts no --before= argument passes a bare (non-@, undivided) nanosecond value, e.g. assert not re.search(r'--before="?\$?\{?[A-Za-z_]*created_at', body_without_the_divided_form).

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Reduce prose-wording coupling in test_sweep_covers_closed_tickets and test_the_choice_between_link_and_resume_has_a_decision_rule — assert the load-bearing artifacts (the executable commands / the --status ALL sweep and the rebar link duplicates command already covered elsewhere) rather than exact bold-label sentences.
evidence: assert "**Open or in progress**" in body
assert "resume that ticket in place" in body
assert "**Closed, and the behavior is back**" in body

These are prose sentences/bold labels, not commands the agent executes nor tokens a downstream parser branches on; rewording (e.g. 'across all statuses, closed included') preserves the guidance but fails the test.
advisory.finding: Several assertions pin exact author PROSE phrasings of an instruction artifact whose sole consumer is an LLM (not a parser/registry), so they are change-detectors: a behavior-preserving reword of the skill's guidance breaks them without any change to what the agent is told to do. Examples: test_sweep_covers_closed_tickets pins the literal 'including closed tickets'; test_the_choice_between_link_and_resume_has_a_decision_rule pins '**Open or in progress**', 'resume that ticket in place', and '**Closed, and the behavior is back**'. Per the Rule-5 litmus, an LLM is not a non-human consumer, so these prose greps guard wording, not a machine-read contract.
